title: Mo Amer and Mehdi Talk Palestine, Comedy, Netflix, and DJ Khaled, LIVE in Houston!
author: Mehdi Hasan
content:
It's been a long time coming, but **Mehdi** was finally joined by the
acclaimed Palestinian-American comedian **Mo Amer** for a very special LIVE
taping of 'We're Not Kidding' in Mo's hometown of Houston, Texas. In this
wide-ranging, hilarious, and, at times, emotional conversation, the two talk
about Mo's groundbreaking Netflix TV series 'Mo', his roots in the Houston
comedy scene, and how the past three years of genocide in Gaza has impacted
him and his community.

**" How hard has the last three years been for you, as a Palestinian public
figure?"** Mehdi asks.

**" I didn't even think about it as a public figure. This has been my life the
whole time," **Mo says. **" The last three years have been heightened by
10,000%."**

[Subscribe now](https://zeteo.com/subscribe)

Mo talks about his family's background in Palestine and growing up in the
melting pot of Houston - the primary inspirations for his Peabody Award-
winning series 'Mo'. Mehdi asks about the series' truly exceptional second
season, which explored ICE detention centers, Israeli cultural appropriation,
and even depicts life for persecuted Palestinians in the occupied West Bank.

**" You see Israeli soldiers just brutalizing Palestinians. And I wonder, how
did you get that past Netflix?" **Mehdi asks.** "This is my own personal
experience. This is what I told them,"** Mo says. **" And this is the nicest
version I could possibly make."**

Mo also gives Mehdi his unfiltered opinion about another famous Palestinian
who has stayed silent on the genocide: DJ Khaled. **" It just feels off and so
disconnected. It feels like you're just playing a version of yourself,"** Mo
says. **" I can't imagine myself constantly being this character. It's just
weird."**

The two also talk about:

  * Mo's first American Halloween as a bewildered immigrant child

  * How Mo got into comedy

  * Being the first Arab-American to sell out Radio City Music Hall

  * Whether James Talarico will turn Texas blue

  * The best places to eat in Houston

  * And they play a Texas-themed version of 'This or That'

They also take questions from the audience of 1,500 people in Houston about
comedy as resistance, the best ways to support the Palestinian diaspora, and
Muslim representation on the stand-up stage.
